portion_doctrine: Photoshop composite photo manipulation tutorial. Video transcript of Nor Arts channel showing step-by-step creation of Stranger Things-inspired dark poster design. Heavily instructional UI/breakdown commentary. Not strategic doctrine or operational blueprint. Primary value: concrete Photoshop technique layer stacking and blending mode application. ~95% raw content is repetitive tutorial narration; 5% actual technical specs extracted below.
operating_rules: Unify all elements to same lightness first before adding effects
Use black background for moody dark designs
Main light source should be brightest point in composition
Mask first, paint secondary (refining edges with soft-rounded brush in mask mode)
Decrease brush flow for subtle control on visible effects
Change blending mode of brush (not layer) to overlay for non-destructive edge refinement on masks
Use clipping masks on every adjustment layer for non-destructive editing
Group related layers and name them (e.g., 'sky', 'buildings', 'kids') for organization
Create adjustment layers for curves, color balance, hue/saturation before adding effects
Paint rim lights to add dimension to subjects
Use hazing/fog layers to add mysteriousness and magic (screen blend mode)
Add camera roll filter at end for final punch
Fade edges with soft brush and decreased flow for smooth transitions
Balance visual weight by adding layers to underweighted areas
Double-layer multiply technique: duplicate layer, set to multiply, use mask to control shadow areas
named_methods: Quick Design Breakdown: Visual reference preview before detailed build
Color + Light + Shadow stacking: Correct colors, then lights, then shadows separately per element
Blending sky & buildings: Create curves adjustment (darken), color balance (add cyan/blue), organize in group
Blending kids/subjects: Correct lightness, add blues, paint shadows separately, then apply effects
Spider masking: Mask eyes to prevent loss in dark areas, use blend-if to remove color from blacks
Blue haze & light effects: Layer fog layers with screen mode, use levels/saturation to refine, paint beam brushes for light trails
Multiply shadow technique: Duplicate source layer, set to multiply mode, mask to show only shadows, decrease opacity for subtlety
